title: Champions League Predictions: PSG, Barcelona in Action; Carrick Fights for Man Utd Job
subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By James CormackNov 2, 2026PSG beat Barcelona in a barnstormer last time out.  / David Ramos/UEFA/Getty ImagesMatchday 4 represents the halfway point in the Champions League league phase, and there’s several heavy-hitters in action in the first round of fixtures.

Only five teams are perfect through three games, including back-to-back winners Paris Saint-Germain, perennial champions Real Madrid, two Premier League teams and ... Real Betis? The Andalusians are enjoying their return to the big time after a two-decade absence, and will continue their campaign on Wednesday against German giants Borussia Dortmund at Signal Iduna Park.

The maintenance of perfection is one of the several intriguing subplots pervading this set of fixtures, although the majority of eyes will undoubtedly be cast on the events that unfold in Manchester and Madrid.
Here’s how Sports Illustrated predicts Tuesday’s Matchday 4 fixtures will pan out.

Winning away from home will ultimately decide how far an ambitious Galatasaray can go in this competition, so they would‘ve been greatly encouraged by their 4–2 triumph at Lille on Matchday 3.
They’ll undoubtedly be feeling good about themselves when they welcome Stuttgart to Istanbul, with the two teams facing off for the first time in a UEFA competition.

Galatasaray haven’t beaten German opposition at home in nine attempts, and the visitors head into Tuesday’s fixture in a buoyant mood themselves. They’ve claimed seven points from their opening three matches, including a 1–1 draw with Atlético Madrid last time out, and were impressively victorious in the Bundesliga on Saturday, winning away at Bayer Leverkusen 4–2.
Shakhtar Donetsk were successful at Stamford Bridge on Matchday 2, bypassing an enthusiastically-supported AEK Athens 3–1 on neutral territory.

The Brazilian-laden Ukrainian outfit offered a good account of themselves at San Siro last time out, only narrowly losing to Inter Milan, two-time finalists this decade. Now they’re taking on a Sporting CP in the midst of a transition, with Paulo Fonseca set to replace Rui Borges as manager.

Sporting were stunned by LASK on Matchday 3, and are already nine points behind Porto in the Primeira Liga title race. They have, however, won all four matches against Ukrainian opposition in this competition.
The Ballon d’Or winner will have to shoulder the load in Madrid. / Alex Grimm/Getty ImagesPrediction: Atlético Madrid 2–1 Bayern Munich

Harry Kane is going to have to carry the load for Bayern Munich in the Spanish capital, given the swathe of injuries the visiting team is dealing with. Der Klassiker was a nightmare occasion for the German champions, who lost Ismael Saibari, Serge Gnabry and Michael Olise to injury.

Kane, who paraded his Ballon d’Or to the Allianz Arena before kick-off, produced a rare errant night in front of goal, missing from the penalty spot as Borussia Dortmund scored a late equalizer to earn a 2–2 draw.

Bayern were pegged back by Arsenal last time out in Europe, and a daunting challenge heads their way this week. Atlético Madrid are in irresistible form, with their unbeaten run across all competitions extending to nine games since they were beaten at Liverpool in September.
Atléti haven’t lost a Champions League home game to German opposition since 1996—a run of 16 matches.
Barcelona bounced back from a difficult week against Alavés.  / David Ramos/Getty ImagesPrediction: Barcelona 3–1 Aston Villa
Barcelona had to bounce back from a difficult week when they welcomed Deportivo Alavés to Camp Nou on Saturday, and Hansi Flick’s team responded by putting six past the out-of-sorts visitors.
Flick interestingly didn’t rotate so much ahead of a challenging run before the international break, with a trip to second-place Atléti up next in La Liga after Aston Villa come to town.

Barça’s first blemish of the season came against the back-to-back champions on Matchday 3, and Villa are one of the five perfect teams approaching the halfway mark. They’ve cruised beyond Fenerbahçe and Viking in their two recent continental duels, but saw their momentum stymied by Fulham at the weekend.
